note: Psychologically the ideal customer and demographically outside the stated definition. Good_to_great is close to perfect — he is buying the last 10-20% of knowledge to break a ceiling, not a rescue — and not_deconditioned is emphatic: trains almost daily by choice, hikes 20 miles a day with a pack, snowboards and climbs. Income holds: debt-free, an 800 credit score, and 'I think 6K is totally doable for me'. He misses on two. Successful, as the ICP defines it, means a business owner, physician or equivalent; he is a salaried account and project manager at a SaaS company, which is a good professional job but not the profile the criterion describes. Neglected_health fails in the opposite direction from the usual: health is not the deprioritised area of his life, it is the most deliberately managed one — daily training, sauna, cold plunge, clean eating, an unintentional five-year intermittent fast, and a promise made to himself twenty years ago to always be in shape. There is nothing here that has been neglected. This is a useful data point for the central comparison: the stated ICP screens on occupation and on health being an unattended problem, and this prospect fails both while being, on every behavioural measure, the lowest-delivery-risk buyer in the batch. It suggests the ICP's occupation and neglect tests are proxies that a direct test of training commitment would beat.
